analysis.title: Midday Market Intelligence: the letter 'e'
key_insights: US stocks traded broadly higher on Tuesday 10/27, led by tech and consumer discretionary, ahead of the scheduled FOMC meeting on Wednesday and MSFT and GOOGL earnings Wednesday night and AMZN Thursday night.

Markets leaned back into the AI infrastructure trade for a second day, with semis and most Mega Cap Tech higher. GS says concerns about peak AI investment and its returns remain, but investors are climbing the wall of worry into hyperscaler (MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN), memory (SK Hynix, Samsung, STX, SNDK) and other (INTC, TER, NXPI, KLAC, ENTG, MPWR) results later this week.

Staples: KO delivered a strong top-line beat on pricing power, emerging-market growth and margin expansion. SFD reported softer-than-expected results on volume and pricing declines across major meat segments. SFD traded up while KO traded lower.
Travel and leisure: RCL, HLT and TNL results point to resilient travel demand. RCL shows stronger pricing momentum and booking visibility than the hotels.
Healthcare: CNC and HCA both reported strong results, but showed the effects of disruption and changing enrollment in health insurance exchanges at both ends of the healthcare delivery chain.

FinTech: PYPL reported stronger-than-expected 3Q results on better transaction margins and lower opex. SOFI beat expectations and raised 2027 guidance on borrowing demand, high origination volumes and better NIM.

Data centers: JCI orders reaccelerated to +44% organic y/y (vs +27% in F3Q26) with backlog of $23.0bn, +43% y/y. XYL saw double-digit order growth in Applied Water on data center cooling demand. AMT beat EBITDA expectations, maintained guidance and flagged softer US organic growth.

Planes and trucks: BA reported better-than-expected FCF and progress on revenue and margin drivers, but still faces higher supply chain costs and is working to stabilize its delivery timeline. UPS reported a beat-and-raise on progress in domestic shipping.

Materials: higher raw material costs weighed on SHW's 3Q results despite strong consumer and professional end markets. FCX reiterated 2026 Grasberg production guidance and lowered 2030 production guidance.

Info services: SPGI beat on revenue and margins and raised FY2026 guidance. Transaction revenue grew 1% (investment grade strength from hyperscaler deals and M&A, offset by softness in high yield, bank loans and structured finance) and non-transaction revenue grew 4%.

The Conference Board October Consumer Confidence survey came in well above expectations, in line with levels from the start of the year. Durable goods orders, ex-transportation orders and core capital goods shipments all rose in September. GS raised its 3Q GDP tracking estimate by 0.1pp to +3.4% qoq annualized.

David Mericle expects the FOMC to skip a hike at Wednesday's meeting and deliver a second hike in December. Market pricing has removed one hike and now peaks at just over 4.5%. GS baseline and probability-weighted Fed forecasts are less hawkish than the market because GS doubts four hikes and expects cuts later.

After the close Tuesday: HOOD, V, FFIV, ACGL, BXP, ESS, EXR, TER, CSGP, VTR, BKR, EQT, FE, OKE, PPG, WM, UHS report. Before the open Wednesday: APH, FLEX, TEL, VRT, FTV, GEV, LII, OTIS, GNRC, GRMN, ADP, BIIB, BSX, GEHC, AON, ETSY, WING and others.

SFD reported 10/27 softer-than-expected results on broad-based volume and pricing declines across major meat segments.
RCL reported 3Q26 on 10/27 with strong pricing momentum and booking visibility. HLT and TNL also reported, pointing to resilient travel demand.
CNC and HCA reported strong 3Q26 results on 10/27, with health insurance exchange enrollment changes affecting both.
PYPL reported 3Q26 on 10/27, stronger than expected on better transaction margins and lower opex.
SOFI reported 3Q26 on 10/27, beat expectations and raised 2027 guidance on borrowing demand, origination volumes and NIM.
JCI reported F4Q26 on 10/27: orders +44% organic y/y (vs +27% in F3Q26), backlog $23.0bn, +43% y/y.
XYL reported on 10/27 with double-digit order growth in Applied Water.
AMT reported 3Q26 on 10/27, beat EBITDA expectations, maintained guidance, and cited softer US organic growth.
BA reported 3Q26 on 10/27 with better-than-expected FCF. UPS reported a beat-and-raise.
